answers.core: This would be part of the standalone command line tools
answers.workaround:
It can be worked around either:
- With a shell script that loops every `.gd` script and calls `godot check-only -s` every time
- By having a separate `.gd` script that is not used by the game, but preloads every other script. You can then use `godot --check-only -s` on that script. If an error is found in one of those preloaded scripts, a parse error is thrown.

title: Allow passing multiple scripts when running in standalone mode with the `--check-only` option
